title: Embeddings & Rerank: configurable PII redaction, retention and audit-event plan
creator: Samir Kapoor
description:
Goal: Implement a configurable privacy layer for the embeddings and reranking endpoints that prevents sensitive customer data from being logged in plain text, provides per-customer retention controls, and emits auditable, minimal events for compliance. This ticket covers the engineering design, an initial implementation behind a feature flag, test harness, and rollout plan for internal beta customers.

Motivation: Several customers (regulated/finance/healthcare) have requested stronger guarantees around PII leakage in embedding vectors and reranking logs. Current logging emits full request payloads to the event stream for troubleshooting which increases exposure risk. We need an approach that: (1) removes or masks PII before any persistent logs, (2) supports short retention windows configurable per-org, and (3) emits a tamper-evident audit event containing only non-identifying metadata and cryptographic hashes where necessary.
acceptance_criteria: Config flag 'emb-privacy-v2' gates new behavior; default off for control plane until rollout
Request payloads containing configured PII patterns are redacted before any synchronous or async logging (no plaintext in logs or metrics)
Retention window enforced: logs created under this code path are automatically TTL'd and deleted per org-config (granular to 1 day, 7 days, 30 days)
Audit events contain request_id, model_version, redaction_summary, and HMACed (KMS-backed) identifiers; no raw PII fields
End-to-end tests prove no plaintext PII is present in persisted logs for sampled requests (1000 synthetic examples)
Latency overhead for embedding requests (single-request median) <= +6ms and p95 <= +20ms vs baseline
Load test at target scale (10k qps synthetic embedding load) shows <5% throughput regression when feature enabled with sampling=1.0
Security review completed and SOC/Compliance checklist updated
technical_design: Redaction strategy: multi-layer approach — (A) deterministic token-level pattern redaction (emails, ssn, credit card), (B) configurable named-entity redaction model pipeline (lightweight NER) for customer-defined types, (C) optional pseudonymization using salted HMAC with per-customer key from KMS for identifiers that must remain linkable

Logging pipeline: introduce a 'privacy sanitizer' middleware in the request path for /embeddings and /rerank that runs before any logger, metrics emitter, or telemetry hook. Middleware must be asynchronous-safe and idempotent

Retention: attach TTL metadata to events written to the log store. Retention enforcement handled by log-store lifecycle jobs; for on-prem/VPC customers where lifecycle can't be enforced centrally, emit a retention-policy header to the local agent and document required agent behavior

Audit event schema (minimal): [request_id, timestamp, org_id, model, route, redaction_summary, hashed_customer_id, redaction_version, config_flags, hmac_signature]. The hashed_customer_id is HMAC(KMS_key, customer_id || salt) and stored only in event stream (no raw id)
KMS integration: use existing KMS client (ENG-14780) to perform signing/HMAC operations. Key access logged and audited via key-usage events
Feature flags & sampling: new flags in runtime config: emb_privacy_mode (off|redact|pseudonymize), emb_privacy_sampling (0.0-1.0). Default: off. Allow per-org override via config API
Backward compatibility: if flag is off, existing behavior unchanged. Telemetry consumers must accept optional redaction_summary and hashed_customer_id fields
Observability: add specific metrics: sanitized_requests.count, sanitized_latency.histogram, sanitized_rejected_patterns.count, kms_hmac_errors.count, retention_policy_applied.count
RBAC: only SEs and support with 'audit-logs' permission can retrieve raw audit-events; redacted logs accessible to broader support team
Storage encryption: events written to long-term store must be encrypted at rest using existing envelope encryption and have per-org key identifiers
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): implement middleware + unit tests behind local flag; PR review and security design review (internal) - target 2 weeks

Phase 1 (internal beta): enable emb-privacy-v2=true and sampling=0.1 for 3 internal orgs (internal-platform, core-platform, few selected enterprise customers) - monitor errors, latency, and false positive redactions for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (partner beta): expand to 10 paying customers with varying compliance needs; collect feedback and update redaction rules and retention UI - 4 weeks
Phase 3 (gradual rollout): default sampling=0.01 and opt-in via console for orgs; after SLA and security signoff flip default to redact mode for new orgs only
Emergency rollback: set emb-privacy-v2=off globally; fallback path preserves original logs and metrics
testing_plan: Unit tests for each redaction pattern and NER pipeline with edge-case inputs (unicode, homoglyphs, concatenated tokens)
Property tests to verify idempotence of redaction (running sanitizer twice yields same result)
Integration test harness that replays 1000 synthetic PII-containing requests through /embeddings and /rerank and asserts no plaintext storage
Performance benchmarks vs baseline at 1, 10, 100 concurrent clients; record median/p95/p99 latency and CPU/GPU impact
Chaos test: simulate KMS latency/failure and verify HMAC errors are safe-fail (log error, fallback to redaction-only, do not block request)
Security pen-test on audit event stream to confirm no residual identifiers; involve security team and one external audit vendor
Automated e2e nightly test that samples production traffic (scrubbed copy) and verifies no PII in persisted logs
notes: Trade-offs considered: Deep model-backed NER reduces false negatives but increases CPU cost and latency; chosen approach prefers lightweight pattern + optional NER for orgs that opt-in

Edge case: embeddings themselves may encode PII in vector space. This ticket focuses on request/response logging and audit trails, not vector sanitization. Follow-up ticket recommended for vector-level differential privacy (ENG-16005)
Related legal ask: compliance wants 90-day default retention for enterprise; engineering will expose per-org policy but default will be 30 days to balance cost

Open question: whether encryption of HMAC-produced hashed_customer_id using per-org envelope key is necessary in addition to KMS HMAC. Proposed: store HMAC only; rotation handled by key-version metadata in event
Coordination: notify Console & RBAC teams to add UI controls for retention and per-org enablement; notify Observability for metrics and dashboards

Potential perf optimization: run light-weight redaction in fast-path and defer expensive NER to background sanitizer that updates audit events asynchronously (helps p95). Must ensure no raw PII is persisted synchronously
updates: 2025-02-11: Drafted initial design and discussed with Security. Security requested explicit HMAC approach and KMS auditability
2025-02-14: Added retention TTL metadata requirement after compliance sync. Marked as P1
2025-02-18: Proof-of-concept middleware completed; local microbenchmarks show +4ms median for embedding single-call; need optimization for p95
2025-02-22: Feature flag schema submitted to runtime config infra (ENG-15231). Added rollout phases and test plan
